Have you looked at the X configuration file before and after you make the changes (or after reboot)?

That would be where I'd start.

  1. boot as you always do and look at the config file
  2. make the change and save the configuration
  3. compare the newly saved file to the original

Okay, they look different. Why would it be resetting the configuration when I log out? I switched the inputs like the other guys suggested, and all that managed to do was make it display the GRUB bootloader on the wrong screen too.

Ok, so saving the configuration file is working. But when you reboot it's back to what #1 looked like?

If so, then something is interfering and we need to figure out what and why.

Let's try this:

http://askubuntu.com/questions/421730/xorg-conf-changes-from-nvidia-setting-have-no-effect-after-reboot

Had the same problem on 13.10 with Nvidia NVS 510 and 4 monitors. Even though nvidia-settings were configured correctly and saved to xorg.conf after reboot rotation options were not remembered.

The solution was to open System Settings → Displays and configure the monitors again in the proper configuration. Then click Apply. I presume that this is what writes to ~/.config/monitors.xml.

After that everything worked fine and persisted after reboot.
This fixed it!! Thank you! I wonder why they would have display configurations stored in two separate files...but that's for someone with a lot more experience to figure out!

With Mint, the idea is that it's a proper desktop system and I think that entails a philosophy of "you shouldn't be digging into text configuration files in a graphically-oriented system." It probably writes the display settings to disk when you shutdown, to make sure they're saved.
Are you running the Nvidia proprietary driver?

I get the same problem when using two monitors with a Nvidia 650ti. Never had the problem before with my previous card. I kept changing the settings and tried switching the cables but nothing worked. After a few weeks of trying to figure it out with no luck I found out what the problem was.

Whichever screen I was using last when I shut down would for some reason become defaulted to the main screen, I had to make sure that my main screen was the only screen with any activity on it before shutting down. If the second screen had any activity on it, for some reason it would default as the main screen.

I haven't been able to figure out why the screen swap happens but that has been my fix for the issue.
Somebody else said to try changing the screen settings in the main Control Panel. I did it, and it worked!
